uv sync --extra dev

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text:
groundworkers supports three steady-state integration styles:

  1. MCP for agentic clients and tool discovery
  2. REST for fixed workflow applications
  3. Direct Python for in-process orchestration

All three reuse the same runtime config, adapters, and services.

docs.title: How to choose
docs.text: If you need... Use... Tool discovery, agent interoperability, remote capability sharing MCP Typed HTTP APIs, OpenAPI, fixed workflow contracts REST Lowest overhead, batch jobs, library composition inside Python Direct Python

docs.title: Shared runtime shape
docs.text: sequenceDiagram     participant C as Consumer     participant T as Transport     participant S as Service     participant A as Adapter     participant D as OMOP / model dependencies      C->>T: request     T->>S: service call     S->>A: dependency call     A->>D: query / API call     D-->>A: raw result     A-->>S: normalized result     S-->>T: domain result     T-->>C: transport response

docs.title: Start the service
docs.text:
Local stdio:

groundworkers

Shared HTTP MCP service:

groundworkers \
  --transport streamable-http \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000

Inspect the active tool surface:

groundworkers --describe

docs.title: Example client workflow
docs.text:
Pseudocode:

bundle = mcp_client.call_tool(
    "concept_candidate_bundle",
    {
        "query": "type 2 diabetes",
        "domain": "Condition",
        "include_normalized": True,
        "include_fulltext": True,
        "include_embedding": True,
        "include_standard_mappings": True,
    },
)

Representative request payload:

{
  "query": "type 2 diabetes",
  "domain": "Condition",
  "include_normalized": true,
  "include_fulltext": true,
  "include_embedding": true,
  "include_standard_mappings": true,
  "include_hierarchy_context": true
}

Representative response shape:

{
  "query": "type 2 diabetes",
  "constraints": {
    "domain": "Condition",
    "vocabulary_id": null,
    "standard_only": false,
    "active_only": true,
    "parent_ids": null
  },
  "channels": {
    "exact": {"available": true, "results": []},
    "normalized": {"available": true, "results": []},
    "fulltext": {"available": true, "results": []},
    "embedding": {"available": true, "results": []}
  },
  "standardized_candidates": [],
  "candidate_union": [],
  "warnings": []
}

MCP is the right interface when the caller wants discoverability and can work in terms of tool names and JSON-ish payloads.

docs.text:
groundworkers \
  --transport rest \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8080

Current curated routes:

  • GET /healthz
  • POST /v1/mapping/candidate-bundle
  • POST /v1/source-planning/assisted-plan

docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/mapping/candidate-bundle \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \

    "query": "type 2 diabetes",

    "include_embedding": true,
    "include_standard_mappings": true

docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/source-planning/assisted-plan \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "content": "field_name,field_label\nhba1c,Haemoglobin A1c\n",

REST is curated rather than exhaustive. The REST transport exposes workflow operations with stable request and response models; it does not attempt to mirror the full MCP tool surface.

docs.text:

docs.title: Example: service-backed mapper
docs.text:
class MappingReviewService:
    def __init__(self, mapping_service) -> None:
        self._mapping = mapping_service

    def build_review_packet(self, source_term: str) -> dict:
        bundle = self._mapping.concept_candidate_bundle(
            source_term,
            domain="Condition",
            include_normalized=True,
            include_fulltext=True,
            include_embedding=True,
            include_standard_mappings=True,
            include_hierarchy_context=True,
        )
        top = bundle["candidate_union"][0] if bundle["candidate_union"] else None
        context = None
        if top is not None:
            context = self._mapping.concept_mapping_context(
                top["concept_id"],
                include_standard_mapping=True,
                include_ancestors=True,
                include_relationship_summary=True,
                include_neighbors=True,
            )
        return {
            "source_term": source_term,
            "bundle": bundle,
            "selected_context": context,
        }

Direct Python is the best fit when your caller is already Python and you want the service layer without a transport hop.

For graph-backed direct Python calls, prefer app.services.graph and app.services.grounding. For lexical retrieval, use app.services.vocab. For review-oriented orchestration, use app.services.mapping.

docs.title: Mixing interfaces
docs.text:
It is reasonable to combine interfaces in one deployment:

  • use MCP for agentic callers
  • use REST for tightly controlled workflow applications
  • use direct Python for batch evaluation, tests, or internal orchestration

Because all three sit on the same service layer, the important choice is consumer ergonomics and transport fit, not a different implementation path.

docs.title: Running tests
docs.text:
# all tests (unit + integration; integration tests are skipped without a live DB)
pytest

# unit tests only (no database required)
pytest tests/unit/

# single file
pytest tests/unit/test_concept_tools.py

docs.title: Test configuration
docs.text:
Integration tests that query the OMOP database require a .env file at the repo root (or an environment-variable equivalent):

OMOP_CDM_DB_URL=postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/omop

Unit tests mock the adapter layer and run without a live database.
